title: Superconstant word-RAM time for prefix-\(U_1\)
formal:
Is it impossible to maintain a length-\(n\) bit sequence under substitutions and answer prefix-AND queries using a deterministic uniform word-RAM data structure with \(O(n)\) preprocessing and \(O(1)\) worst-case time for each update and each query?

An update \(\operatorname{set}(i,b)\) replaces the bit at position \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) by \(b\in\{0,1\}\). A query at \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) must return
\[\operatorname{prefix}(k)=\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k}b_i,\qquad\operatorname{prefix}(0)=1.\]
The word length is \(w=\lceil c\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) for a fixed integer constant \(c\ge1\). The impossibility is to hold for every such fixed constant and every correct data structure in the model below.

This retains the source's worst-case time convention. The target is absence of any constant bound, not a prescribed logarithmic lower-bound rate or the stronger exclusion of amortized constant time.

source_formulation.text: There is no structure for prefix-U1 with complexity \(O(1)\).
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 6

why: This small dynamic problem isolates whether maintaining even threshold information about a changing minimum requires more than a constant number of actual word operations. Its hardness would complete conditional classifications of dynamic regular-language membership, and newer work extends that connection to tree languages. The challenge concerns computation inside the machine as well as memory access, making it a foundational word-RAM question.

sentences: The prefix-U-one problem maintains a fixed-length bit sequence under substitutions and returns the AND of any requested prefix.
The conjecture rules out a deterministic data structure with linear preprocessing and constant worst-case time for both operations.
Its machine has logarithmic-size words and explicitly charged arithmetic, bit operations and memory accesses.
Amortized constant time, expected constant time and stronger predecessor queries are separate questions.
A resolution would settle a basic dynamic set barrier underlying conditional classifications for regular word and tree languages.

definitions:
The sequence length \(n\ge1\) remains fixed for the lifetime of the structure. Its initial bits are supplied explicitly, one per input cell. Preprocessing receives \(n\) and that sequence and must run in at most \(K(n+1)\) word operations for one fixed constant \(K\). It builds the state from which all subsequent operations are served. The two-element monoid \(U_1=\{0,1\}\) has multiplication Boolean AND, with identity one and absorbing element zero. Hence a nonempty prefix has product zero exactly when it contains a zero.

Equivalently, the zero positions form a changing subset \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Substitution adds or removes a supplied position, and the complemented prefix answer says whether \(S\cap\{1,\ldots,k\}\) is nonempty. Repeating a substitution with the present value is allowed and must also meet the cost bound. Queries do not ask for the minimum element itself or a predecessor of the query position. No insertion or deletion of sequence positions, change of \(n\), or restriction on which positions may change is included.

Use a finite-program unit-cost random-access machine whose cells and addresses are unsigned \(w\)-bit words. One operation can read or write one addressed cell, copy a word, compare two words or branch, apply word addition, subtraction or multiplication, apply unsigned integer division or remainder by a nonzero word, apply bitwise AND, OR, XOR or NOT, or shift a word left or right by a supplied integer amount. Arithmetic results are reduced modulo \(2^w\), except that division and remainder have their usual unsigned integer meanings; left shifts discard overflowing bits, right shifts insert zeros, and shifts by at least \(w\) give zero. Division by zero must be avoided or handled as an error, not an extra operation. Constant literals are fixed by the finite program. The program can use \(n\) and \(w\); both are supplied at initialization. Each listed operation has unit cost. No other arbitrary word function or input-dependent instruction is provided.

There are at most \(2^w\) addressable cells, all initially zero except the supplied input. Every read, write and table construction counts; no nonuniform precomputed table or advice depending on \(n\) is supplied free of charge. There is no additional linear-space requirement: the machine may use its polynomially many addressable cells, even if many were populated by previous updates. The fixed program, positive integer \(c\) and preprocessing constant \(K\) may depend on the data structure, but never on the input length, initial bits or future history. These explicit word operations instantiate the source's unit-cost arithmetic RAM convention, with only logarithmically many bits per word.

Updates and queries arrive one at a time. The answer to each query must be exactly correct for the state after all earlier updates, before a later operation is revealed. Every finite operation history is allowed, including histories selected using earlier answers and histories much longer than \(n\). All operation invocations must terminate. The structure is deterministic, with no error probability and no random or expected-time convention.

A constant-time structure would have one constant \(T\) bounding the work of every individual update and query, for every initial sequence, every length and every history. The work done by one operation cannot be charged to earlier or later operations. Allowing an onset \(n_0\) rather than all lengths gives the same existence question, since the finitely many smaller lengths can be handled separately. Consequently a positive impossibility result can be expressed as follows: for every correct linear-preprocessing structure, every proposed bound \(B\) and every onset \(N\), there is a length \(n\ge N\), an initial sequence and a finite operation history in which an individual operation takes more than \(B\) steps. No particular function tending to infinity is prescribed in advance.

The cell-probe model, mentioned in the context, charges only memory accesses and allows arbitrary computation on values already read at no cost. It is more permissive than the word-operation model just defined; a counting argument that ignores all such computation cannot automatically establish the requested word-RAM barrier.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the claimed nonexistence. A proof must exclude every correct deterministic uniform structure with linear preprocessing and fixed logarithmic word-length constant from having a common constant worst-case bound for both operations. It may give a quantitative lower bound, but must justify that it excludes all constants in this model. A refutation must give a single finite-program structure, some fixed word-length constant, linear preprocessing and exact constant worst-case bounds for both updates and queries on every history. An amortized or expected constant upper bound alone does not refute the specified worst-case conjecture. A lower bound for a stronger query task, larger monoid, smaller instruction set or stricter space limit does not alone prove it.

context_blocks.text: Section 2 explicitly uses worst-case operation cost and linear preprocessing. The question concerns the two-element AND monoid. The separately discussed three-element monoid has a stronger predecessor-type task and a different known lower bound.

The source records an \(O(\log\log n)\) deterministic upper bound and a better expected bound when randomness is allowed. It emphasizes that this does not provide the superconstant lower bound and distinguishes the word-RAM problem from unrestricted local computation in the cell-probe model.

The 2022 string-data-structure paper formulates a stronger amortized constant-time hardness conjecture. Its conditional consequences are evidence of the primitive’s relevance, but this card retains the original worst-case question rather than silently changing the cost convention.

The 2025 tree-language paper still states prefix-U-one hardness as a conjectural premise. Under that premise it classifies constant-time maintainability for its specified class of regular tree languages with a neutral letter; it does not prove the premise.
